title: DiabAgent: Toward Agentic Physiological Control
abstract: arXiv:2611.03601v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: As pretraining scales, medical language models have advanced rapidly in clinical question answering. Their ability to achieve effective physiological control through sustained intervention still lacks systematic quantitative evaluation. Type 1 diabetes provides a concrete setting: impaired insulin secretion creates dependence on exogenous insulin, with dosing continually adjusted using information about meals, exercise, illness, and glucose measurements. We introduce DiabAgent, a research suite for agentic physiological control comprising the Agentic Physiological Control (APC) framework, the DiabetSim simulator, and the SweetBench benchmark. APC controls glucose through medical-device tools, using ongoing observations to infer individual states, accumulate personal experience, and choose treatment actions. We build DiabetSim to simulate different patients, events, and device conditions for scalable virtual testing and training. Using

translated_title: DiabAgent：迈向智能体化生理控制
translated_abstract: 随着预训练规模的不断扩大，医学语言模型在临床问答方面取得了快速进展，但它们通过持续干预实现有效生理控制的能力仍缺乏系统性的定量评估。1型糖尿病为此提供了一个具体的研究场景：胰岛素分泌受损导致患者依赖外源性胰岛素，其剂量需要根据饮食、运动、疾病和血糖测量等信息持续调整。我们提出了DiabAgent，一个面向智能体化生理控制的研究套件，包含三个部分：智能体生理控制（APC）框架、DiabetSim模拟器和SweetBench基准测试。APC通过医疗设备工具控制血糖，利用持续观测来推断个体状态、积累个人经验并选择治疗动作。我们构建了DiabetSim来模拟不同的患者、事件和设备条件，以实现可扩展的虚拟测试与训练。
tldr: 本文提出DiabAgent研究套件，通过APC智能体生理控制框架、DiabetSim糖尿病模拟器和SweetBench基准，首次系统性地实现并定量评估了医学智能体在1型糖尿病血糖持续控制中的能力。
en_tdlr: This paper introduces DiabAgent, a research suite comprising the APC framework, DiabetSim simulator, and SweetBench benchmark, which for the first time enables and systematically quantitatively evaluates agentic physiological control for sustained glucose management in type 1 diabetes.
